In the coordinates (s,t,v) the volume Jacobian is t. For u=t−H(s)/j, the floor u+e^(−j) and t≤u+2/j give the asserted bounded reciprocal integral and uniformly integrable bulk log. The limiting volume is 1/2 and the ordinary raw log mean is 2∫_0^1t log t dt=−1/2.

At a fixed rate the level and its admissibility inequality follow by solving c_j(u+e^(−j))=e^(−rj/ρ). On r≥r_0>0 the t-Jacobian after changing to r is bounded and tends before its indicator to 2H/(cρ). Below ρ the indicator tends to 1_E and above ρ to zero. Uniform domination on a positive-rate neighborhood excludes an atom at ρ and the pointwise slice convergence supplies the stated canonical density.

The bottom parameterization has cross-product norm (A/j)sqrt(2+(A'/j)^2). On E its logarithm is j−log c_j and away from E it is only O(log j) at fixed s. The stated normal and dominated limit give the exterior formula. Every other face has uniformly integrable log by the same u change of variable. The radial factor t_o/sqrt(2) and M=1/2 give exactly the same spatial rate law.

Independent fraction arithmetic gives left/right masses 39/200 and 399/20000, moments 29/3000 and 59551/3000000, mean 9839/71650 and right cap fraction 133/1433. The mean is strictly in the gap. For b=a^2 the leading moment and mass are 3a^2 and 2a, respectively. The cap fraction tends to zero and this mean remains in the gap for sufficiently small a.

An affine marginal of a positive uniform convex-body law has support equal to the affine image of the whole body because the interior is dense and has positive volume in every neighborhood that meets it. This support is convex, whereas E is disconnected. The ordinary scope is one geometric group; no canonical source-base stationarity is used.
